subject: Post-call recap & bakeoff readiness — Ledgerflow evaluation
messages:
From: Emma Rivera <emma@ledgerflow.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + demo — quick recap, pain & current stack

Thanks for the call earlier today, Karthik — appreciate the concise walkthrough. 

Quick recap from our side and the key pain points we asked you to validate: 
- User-facing chat latency spikes during peak hours (p95 spikes above 1s for ~700 token interactions).
- Embedding costs are rising as we scale vector DB (we send batch jobs for nightly re-embeds).
- Model output instability after prompt-tuning: drift on slot-filling prompts introduced noise.
- Security: need private deployment option (no model data leaves VPC) and audit logs for vendor risk team.

Current stack:
- Inference: vLLM on k8s for chat; a small set of TGI endpoints for larger batch jobs (hosted via a managed cloud provider).
- Vector DB: self-hosted Milvus cluster, nightly reindex job.
- Orchestration: Airflow for scheduled embedding runs.

Success criteria we want to use for a bakeoff:
- Latency: p50 <120ms, p95 <400ms for 512-token chat workloads under realistic concurrency.
- Throughput: sustain 150 req/s peak for shorter prompts (<=256 tokens) and 40 req/s for 2k-token flows.
- Cost: target <= $18 / 1M tokens (generation + embeddings combined) on average, or clear path to that with quantization/batching/caching.
- Quality: no regression vs our current baseline on the slot-fill test set (F1 within 1.5%).
- Security: private deployment option + KMS integration + exportable audit logs.

Next steps we discussed:
1) You to share a bakeoff checklist and the test harness we should run against our baseline (we need to validate vLLM/TGI/cloud endpoints too).
2) We’ll share a representative prompt set, token distribution, and a small sample dataset for slot-fill + embedding recall tests.
3) Align on timeline: Ledgerflow target = run experiments week of 03/22 and decision by end of April.

I’ve cc'd procurement for early redline visibility. 

Regards,
Emma Rivera
Senior ML Platform Lead
Ledgerflow Inc.

---

On Mon, Mar 15, 2027 at 6:05 PM Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> wrote:

> Subject: Re: Intro + demo — quick recap, pain & next steps (bakeoff scope)
>
> Hi Emma — great to connect. Below is a concise recap from our side and a concrete proposal for the bakeoff so we all have alignment.
>
> Summary of pain & goals (as we heard them):
> - Reduce chat p95 spikes and overall token cost while preserving or improving extraction/slot-fill accuracy.
> - Reduce embedding unit costs and improve recall for near-real-time retrieval.
> - Ensure a private-hosted option with KMS + auditability for compliance.
>
> Proposed bakeoff scope (Redwood):
> - Baselines: your current vLLM k8s deployment + TGI cloud endpoints (you mentioned both are in use).
> - Redwood configs to test: Hosted API (for POV) + Dedicated pool + Private deployment (VPC) — run equivalent workloads.
> - Variants per config: baseline FP16, int8 quantized, with/without prefix cache, and batching policies tuned to your token distribution.
>
> Acceptance metrics (suggested concrete numbers to run):
> - Chat latency: p50/p95 for 512-token prompts; target p50 <120ms, p95 <400ms under target concurrency.
> - Cold-start: warm vs cold response time delta for first token < 150ms overhead.
> - Throughput: tokens/sec and sustained requests/sec at concurrency=8, 16; target sustained throughput as you requested.
> - Embeddings: recall@10 on your embedding test set (compare to current Milvus retrieval baseline).
> - Cost model: provide modeled cost per 1M tokens for each configuration including amortized infra; show delta vs current stack.
> - Quality: run your slot-fill F1 and a small human-eval subset for hallucination rate.
>
> Deliverables we’ll provide:
> - Redwood bakeoff checklist + test harness (python script + container) you can run in your env or we can run against a staging endpoint.
> - Pre-configured model variants and kernel choices we believe will match your workload.
> - A draft SOW for Dedicated/Private options (attached).
>
> Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-checklist.xlsx (checklist + metrics), SOW-draft-v1.docx (high level).
>
> Proposed timeline:
> - 03/17: Ledgerflow shares test prompts, token histograms, and sample datasets.
> - 03/22–03/26: Run bakeoff experiments (can be executed by both teams; we can also run hosted endpoints against your test harness).
> - 03/29: Share consolidated results and recommendation.
>
> Owner assignments:
> - Karthik (sales lead): coordination and results review.
> - Marissa (solutions engineering): infra config & run ownership.
> - Sergio (account exec): commercial/contract discussion.
>
> Let me know if these acceptance numbers look reasonable or if you want us to tighten any targets before the test runs. Happy to hop on a 30-min sync if that helps finalize the checklist.
>
> Best,
>Karthik Iyer
>Account Executive, Redwood Inference
>

Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prep notes — infra/config & test harness

Karthik / team — adding quick internal runbook items so we don’t miss anything on the bakeoff execution: 

1) Test artifacts we need from Ledgerflow (Emma): prompt set (n=300 representative), token distribution CSV, slot-fill test set + gold labels, embedding evaluation corpus (sample ~50k vectors).
2) Test harness: provide dockerized runner (we’ll build if they can’t run it) + k6 script for concurrency patterns.
3) Infra configs: exact kernel/kernels (GPU type), quantization paths to run (int8 calibration steps), and KV cache settings — I’ll own mapping tables and the infra runbook.
4) Data access: request short-term test account credentials or staging endpoints so we can run against their Milvus index for parity testing.
5) Legal/procurement: Sergio to pre-share our draft SOW so procurement can start redlines.

I’ll prepare three Redwood configs (hosted, dedicated, private) and enumerate the exact commands to reproduce each benchmark. I’ll also include a results template so we can capture p50/p95, tokens/sec, cost estimates, and quality metrics. 

Marissa
Solutions Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
